method: Clip and transition durations accept decimal seconds, mm:ss or hh:mm:ss with at most three decimal places, from 0.001 through 86,400 seconds for clips and 0 through 86,400 seconds for transitions. The frame rate is 1-240 fps with at most three decimal places. Every duration is independently multiplied by the frame rate and rounded to the nearest whole frame; clips rounding below one frame are rejected. One transition is required per adjacent clip pair, with blank or zero rows representing straight cuts. Finished frame count is the sum of clip frames minus the sum of overlap frames. Each later clip starts at the previous clip's end minus their shared overlap. An overlap must be shorter than both adjacent clips, and a clip's incoming plus outgoing overlaps must be shorter than that clip, preventing non-monotonic or triple-overlap timelines. Up to 100 clips are supported. Labels are optional, whitespace-normalized and limited to 80 characters. Displayed times are derived from whole frames and rounded to milliseconds; this is not drop-frame SMPTE timecode, a transition renderer or a media inspector. Nothing is stored or transmitted.
